encounterAtDeath.name: fallen fruit
encounterAtDeath.seen: A soft fallen fruit lies among leaves, bruised but rich with sugar.
encounterAtDeath.cardDetail: The skin is split and damp with sugar scent; insects are already feeding at the torn edge.
investigationDetails: The bruised flesh smells sweet, not rotten. Tiny insects are already feeding in the split skin.
The fruit is soft enough to eat quickly, but the scent will not stay private for long.
This is good fuel, especially for a group, but lingering over it may advertise you.
encounterAtDeath.investigated: The smell is sweet rather than sour. Insects are feeding freely on the torn flesh.

encounterAtDeath.name: bird nest
encounterAtDeath.seen: A small nest rests in the fork of a branch. Pale eggs show through the weave of leaves and twigs.
encounterAtDeath.investigated: The eggs are easy to reach, but feeding here carries smell and noise farther than you want.

encounterAtDeath.name: purple berries
encounterAtDeath.seen: Dark purple berries hang in a small cluster, several already pecked by birds.
investigationDetails: Several berries are torn open by small beaks. Other animals have risked them before you.
The juice smells clean and sweet rather than bitter. This looks like useful food.
The safest berries are the damaged ones: they prove something else ate and moved on.
encounterAtDeath.investigated: Bird marks and torn skins suggest these are likely edible.

encounterAtDeath.name: strangler fig fruit
encounterAtDeath.seen: Small fig fruits cluster from a vine-wrapped trunk, with droppings and peck marks below.
investigationDetails: The ground below is messy with skins and droppings. Many animals feed here.
The fruits are small but numerous. Good group food, though not very filling alone.
Heavy feeding signs mean safety from poison, not safety from attention.
encounterAtDeath.investigated: Common, shared rainforest food. Safe-looking, but it attracts company.

deathContext.message: You collapse from loss of fitness.

encounterAtDeath.name: hairy caterpillar
encounterAtDeath.seen: A hairy caterpillar feeds along the edge of a leaf.
encounterAtDeath.investigated: The hairs are a bad sign. It might be edible, but it may punish the attempt.

encounterAtDeath.name: large eagle
encounterAtDeath.seen: High above the canopy, a broad-winged raptor turns on warm air, searching for the smallest mistake below.
encounterAtDeath.investigated: The large eagle is not behaving like easy prey. Its size, posture, or stillness suggests serious danger.

encounterAtDeath.name: small multituberculate
encounterAtDeath.seen: A small mammal darts between leaves. Its body is small, but its teeth are not harmless.
encounterAtDeath.investigated: The small multituberculate is alert and ready to flee. It may be food, but it will not wait long.

deathContext.message: Gastornis kills you on the forest floor.

encounter.name: Gastornis
encounter.seen: A huge flightless bird steps between the trees, heavy beak lowering toward the forest floor.
encounter.cardDetail: Each step is heavy and deliberate. On open ground, hesitation is what this bird is waiting for.
investigationDetails: It is not stalking delicately; it does not need to. On the ground, its reach and mass make the rules simple.
The beak turns side to side as it searches the leaf litter. Small animals survive this by not being on the floor when it arrives.
The huge bird is not unbeatable in the abstract. For you, here, now, it is the wrong scale of problem.
encounter.investigated: Too large to fight and too dangerous to test on the ground. Climb, hide, or leave.
